animal_cell_v1.title: Animal Cell
animal_cell_v1.summary: The basic unit of life in animals. Each part inside, called an organelle, has its own job.
animal_cell_v1.fidelity_note: Schematic model: shapes and colours are simplified and not to scale. Real cells vary a lot.

components.label: Cell membrane
components.description: A thin, flexible skin around the cell. It decides what goes in and out.
components.function: Controls what enters and leaves the cell.
facts: It is made of two layers of fat-like molecules (a lipid bilayer).

components.label: Cytoplasm
components.description: The jelly-like fluid filling the cell, where the organelles float and many reactions happen.
components.function: Holds the organelles; many chemical reactions happen here.

components.label: Nucleus
components.description: The control centre. It holds most of the cell's DNA, the instructions for building and running the cell.
components.function: Stores DNA and controls the cell's activities.
facts: It is wrapped in a double membrane with pores.

components.label: Nucleolus
components.description: A dense spot inside the nucleus where ribosomes start to be made.

components.label: Mitochondria
components.description: The powerhouses of the cell. They release energy from food (glucose) using oxygen, in cellular respiration.
facts: They have their own small loop of DNA.
Muscle cells have many of them.

components.label: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
components.description: Folded membranes dotted with ribosomes. Proteins are made and folded here.

components.label: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
components.description: Tube-like membranes without ribosomes. They make fats (lipids) and help remove poisons.

components.label: Golgi apparatus
components.description: A stack of flat sacs that packs proteins into little bubbles (vesicles) and sends them where they are needed.

components.label: Ribosomes
components.description: Tiny grains that read instructions from DNA's messages and build proteins.

components.label: Lysosomes
components.description: Small bags of digestive enzymes that break down waste and worn-out parts.

components.label: Centrosome (centrioles)
components.description: A pair of tiny tubes near the nucleus that help pull chromosomes apart when the cell divides.

apollo11_cm_si_v1.title: Apollo 11 Command Module 'Columbia'
apollo11_cm_si_v1.summary: The capsule that carried Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins to the Moon and back in July 1969. It is the only part of the spacecraft that returned to Earth.
apollo11_cm_si_v1.fidelity_note: A 3D scan of the real museum object (Smithsonian). It is one piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

apollo_lm_nasa_v1.title: Apollo Lunar Module
apollo_lm_nasa_v1.summary: The spacecraft that landed astronauts on the Moon between 1969 and 1972. Its bottom half stayed on the Moon; the top half flew the astronauts back up to their command module.

atom_carbon_v1.title: Carbon Atom (Bohr model)
atom_carbon_v1.summary: A carbon atom: 6 protons and 6 neutrons in the nucleus, and 6 electrons arranged 2 and 4 in shells.
atom_carbon_v1.fidelity_note: The Bohr model is a simplified picture. Electrons do not really travel on neat circular paths; quantum physics describes them as clouds of probability. Sizes are hugely exaggerated: a real nucleus is about 100,000 times smaller than the atom.

components.label: Nucleus
components.description: The tiny, heavy centre of the atom, made of protons and neutrons.
components.function: Holds almost all of the atom's mass.

components.label: Protons (6)
components.description: Positively charged particles in the nucleus. Their number, 6, is what makes this atom carbon.

components.label: Neutrons (6)
components.description: Particles with no charge in the nucleus. 6 protons + 6 neutrons = mass number 12.

components.label: K shell (2 electrons)
components.description: The first shell, closest to the nucleus. It is full with 2 electrons.

components.label: L shell (4 electrons)
components.description: The second shell. Carbon has 4 electrons here, its valence electrons, so it forms 4 bonds.

components.label: Electrons (6)
components.description: Very light, negatively charged particles around the nucleus.

bell_x1_si_v1.title: Bell X-1 'Glamorous Glennis'
bell_x1_si_v1.summary: The rocket plane in which Chuck Yeager first flew faster than the speed of sound, on 14 October 1947.
bell_x1_si_v1.fidelity_note: A 3D scan of the real museum object (Smithsonian). It is one piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

black_hole_v1.title: Black Hole
black_hole_v1.summary: A place where so much mass is squeezed into so small a space that gravity lets nothing escape, not even light. Many form when a very big star runs out of fuel and collapses.
black_hole_v1.fidelity_note: Schematic model: a black hole itself cannot be seen. This shows how scientists picture one and the glowing gas around it; sizes and colours are illustrative.

components.label: Event horizon
components.description: The edge of the black hole. Anything that crosses it, even light, can never get back out. It is not a solid surface; it is a point of no return.
components.function: Marks the boundary nothing escapes from.
facts: A black hole with the Sun's mass would have an event horizon only about 6 km across.

components.label: Photon sphere
components.description: At one and a half times the horizon's size, gravity is so strong that light itself can travel in a circle around the black hole.

components.label: Accretion disk
components.description: Gas and dust spiralling inwards. Rubbing and squeezing heat it to millions of degrees, so it glows brightly, mostly in X-rays. Gas closer in orbits faster.
components.function: Feeds the black hole, and is what we actually see.
facts: Gas can orbit steadily only down to about 3 times the horizon's radius; closer than that it plunges in.

components.label: Bent light (lensing)
components.description: Gravity bends light. Light from the far side of the disk is bent over the top and under the bottom of the black hole, so we see the back of the disk as a glowing ring.
facts: The first photo of a black hole (M87*, 2019) shows exactly this: a bright ring around a dark shadow.

components.label: Jets
components.description: Some black holes shoot two narrow beams of particles out from their poles at nearly the speed of light. The jets can stretch for thousands of light years.

blood_cells_v1.title: Human Blood Cells
blood_cells_v1.summary: Blood is a liquid (plasma) carrying red cells, white cells and platelets.
blood_cells_v1.fidelity_note: Schematic model: sizes are roughly in proportion (red cell about 7.5 µm, white cell 10-15 µm, platelet 2-3 µm); shapes and colours simplified.

components.label: Red blood cells
components.description: Disc-shaped cells, dented in the middle, full of haemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to the body.
facts: They have no nucleus.
They live about 120 days.

components.label: White blood cells
components.description: Larger cells with a nucleus that fight germs and protect the body from infection.
facts: Some swallow germs; others make antibodies.

components.label: Platelets
components.description: Tiny cell fragments that clump together to plug a cut and help blood clot.

components.label: Plasma
components.description: The pale yellow liquid part of blood. It carries dissolved food, salts, hormones and waste.
facts: About 55% of blood is plasma.

brain_bp3d_v1.title: Human Brain
brain_bp3d_v1.fidelity_note: Anatomical model (BodyParts3D). Colours are a teaching convention.

components.label: Ventricles (fluid-filled spaces)
components.description: Four connected spaces deep in the brain, filled with cerebrospinal fluid. The fluid cushions the brain and carries away waste.

components.label: Frontal lobe
components.description: The front of the cerebrum. It plans, decides, controls behaviour and speech, and its back strip (the motor cortex) starts voluntary movements.

components.label: Parietal lobe
components.description: The top-back of the cerebrum. It receives touch, pain, heat and body position from the skin and muscles (the sensory cortex) and works out where things are.

components.label: Occipital lobe
components.description: The back of the cerebrum. It receives signals from the eyes and makes sense of what we see.

components.label: Temporal lobe
components.description: The side of the cerebrum, near the ears. It handles hearing, understanding speech, and forming memories.

components.label: Insula
components.description: A lobe hidden deep in the fold between the frontal and temporal lobes; it senses the body's inside state, such as hunger and heartbeat.

components.label: Cingulate gyrus and hippocampus (limbic)
components.description: Inner parts of the cerebrum, round its middle. The hippocampus forms new memories; with the cingulate gyrus they are part of the limbic system, involved in emotion.

components.label: Inner cerebrum (white matter, basal nuclei)
components.description: Under the folded surface: nerve fibres (white matter) joining the parts of the brain, and groups of nerve cells deep inside (the basal nuclei).

components.label: Hypothalamus
components.description: A small region at the base of the forebrain that controls body temperature, hunger, thirst and sleep, and tells the pituitary gland what to do.

components.label: Pineal gland
components.description: A tiny gland in the middle of the brain that makes melatonin, the hormone that helps set the sleep-wake cycle.

components.label: Pituitary gland
components.description: A pea-sized gland hanging below the hypothalamus. Its hormones control growth and many other glands, which is why it is called the master gland.

components.label: Midbrain
components.description: The top of the brainstem. It relays signals for seeing and hearing and helps control eye movements and reflexes.

components.label: Pons
components.description: The bulge in the brainstem below the midbrain. It links the cerebrum with the cerebellum and helps control breathing.

components.label: Medulla oblongata
components.description: The lowest part of the brainstem, joining the spinal cord. It controls involuntary actions: heartbeat, breathing, blood pressure, swallowing, vomiting.

components.label: Cerebellum
components.description: The 'little brain' at the back, under the cerebrum. It keeps balance and posture and makes movements smooth and precise.

components.label: Spinal cord (top)
components.description: The bundle of nerves running down from the medulla inside the backbone, carrying messages between the brain and the body. Shown: its first few centimetres.

cassini_nasa_v1.title: Cassini–Huygens Spacecraft
cassini_nasa_v1.summary: Cassini orbited Saturn from 2004 to 2017, studying its rings and moons. It carried the Huygens probe, which landed on Saturn's moon Titan.

chandra_si_v1.title: Chandra X-ray Observatory
chandra_si_v1.summary: A space telescope that sees X-rays from very hot places such as exploding stars and matter falling into black holes. It is named after the Indian-American scientist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar.
chandra_si_v1.fidelity_note: A 3D scan of the real museum object (Smithsonian). It is one piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

digestive_bp3d_v1.title: Human Digestive System
digestive_bp3d_v1.fidelity_note: Anatomical model (BodyParts3D). Colours are a teaching convention.

components.label: Oesophagus (food pipe)
components.description: A muscular tube that pushes swallowed food down to the stomach by waves of squeezing (peristalsis).

components.label: Stomach
components.description: A muscular bag that churns food with acid and enzymes, turning it into a thick liquid.

components.label: Liver
components.description: The largest gland in the body. It makes bile, which helps digest fats, and stores and cleans many substances in the blood.

components.label: Gall bladder
components.description: A small bag under the liver that stores bile and squeezes it into the small intestine.

components.label: Pancreas
components.description: Makes digestive juice for the small intestine, and the hormone insulin that controls blood sugar.

components.label: Caecum
components.description: A pouch where the small intestine joins the large intestine.

components.label: Appendix
components.description: A small finger-shaped tube on the caecum. In humans it has no major role in digestion.

components.label: Duodenum
components.description: The first part of the small intestine, where bile and pancreatic juice join the food.

components.label: Jejunum
components.description: The middle part of the small intestine, where most digested food is absorbed into the blood.

components.label: Ileum
components.description: The last part of the small intestine. Finger-like villi on its inner wall absorb nutrients.

components.label: Colon (large intestine)
components.description: The large intestine absorbs water and salts from what is left, forming solid waste.

components.label: Rectum
components.description: Stores waste until it leaves the body through the anus.

earth_nasa_v1.title: Planet Earth
earth_nasa_v1.summary: Our home planet, the third from the Sun. About 71% of its surface is covered by water.
earth_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: Earth
components.description: Our home planet, the third from the Sun. About 71% of its surface is covered by water.
facts: Its axis is tilted by about 23.4°, which gives us the seasons.
It spins once a day and goes round the Sun once a year.

europa_nasa_v1.title: Europa (moon of Jupiter)
europa_nasa_v1.summary: An icy moon of Jupiter. Under its cracked ice shell there is probably a salty ocean, one of the best places to look for life.
europa_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: Europa (moon of Jupiter)
components.description: An icy moon of Jupiter. Under its cracked ice shell there is probably a salty ocean, one of the best places to look for life.

eye_bp3d_v1.title: Human Eye
eye_bp3d_v1.fidelity_note: Anatomical model (BodyParts3D). Colours are a teaching convention.

components.label: Cornea
components.description: The clear dome at the front of the eye. It bends (refracts) light more than any other part.

components.label: Iris
components.description: The coloured ring. Its muscles make the hole in the middle (the pupil) smaller in bright light and bigger in dim light.

components.label: Lens
components.description: A clear, flexible lens behind the iris. It changes shape to focus near or far objects onto the retina.

components.label: Suspensory ligaments
components.description: Fine fibres that hold the lens in place and pull on it to change its shape.

components.label: Vitreous humour
components.description: The clear jelly filling the eyeball, keeping its round shape.

components.label: Choroid
components.description: A dark layer full of blood vessels that feeds the eye. Behind it the retina (not modelled here) turns light into nerve signals.

components.label: Sclera
components.description: The tough white outer coat that protects the eyeball.

galileo_nasa_v1.title: Galileo Spacecraft
galileo_nasa_v1.summary: Orbited Jupiter from 1995 to 2003 and found signs of a salty ocean under the ice of the moon Europa.

gemini_nasa_v1.title: Gemini Spacecraft
gemini_nasa_v1.summary: NASA's two-person spacecraft of 1965–66. Gemini missions practised spacewalks and docking, skills needed to reach the Moon.

heart_bp3d_v1.title: Human Heart
heart_bp3d_v1.fidelity_note: Anatomical model (BodyParts3D). Colours are a teaching convention.

components.label: Aortic valve
components.description: Semilunar valve with three cusps between the left ventricle and the aorta. It opens when the left ventricle contracts and closes to stop blood flowing back.

components.label: Pulmonary valve
components.description: Semilunar valve with three cusps between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk.

components.label: Tricuspid valve
components.description: Valve with three leaflets between the right atrium and right ventricle. It closes when the ventricle contracts, so blood cannot flow back into the atrium.

components.label: Mitral valve
components.description: Valve with two leaflets (the bicuspid valve) between the left atrium and left ventricle. Shown with its fibrous ring.

components.label: Right atrium
components.description: Receives deoxygenated blood from the body through the superior and inferior venae cavae, and passes it to the right ventricle.

components.label: Left atrium
components.description: Receives oxygenated blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins, and passes it to the left ventricle.

components.label: Right ventricle
components.description: Pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk, on its way to the lungs.

components.label: Left ventricle
components.description: Pumps oxygenated blood through the aortic valve into the aorta and out to the whole body. It has the thickest muscular wall of the four chambers.

components.label: Aorta
components.description: The largest artery, carrying oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body. Shown: the ascending aorta and the aortic arch.

components.label: Pulmonary trunk
components.description: Carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle towards the lungs, where it divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries (not shown).

components.label: Superior vena cava
components.description: Returns deoxygenated blood from the head, neck and arms to the right atrium.

components.label: Inferior vena cava
components.description: Returns deoxygenated blood from the lower body to the right atrium. Shown: its last few centimetres before the heart.

components.label: Pulmonary veins
components.description: Carry oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium; usually four, two from each lung. Shown: the parts outside the lungs.

components.label: Coronary arteries
components.description: The right and left coronary arteries and their branches, which supply the heart muscle itself with oxygenated blood.

components.label: Cardiac veins
components.description: Veins that drain the heart muscle, mostly into the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium.

hubble_nasa_v1.title: Hubble Space Telescope
hubble_nasa_v1.summary: A telescope orbiting Earth since 1990, above the blurring air, taking very sharp pictures of planets, stars and galaxies.
hubble_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: NASA's 3D model of Hubble. It is one solid piece, so you can turn and zoom it but not pick separate parts.

ingenuity_nasa_v1.title: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
ingenuity_nasa_v1.summary: The first aircraft to fly on another planet (2021). Mars's air is very thin, so its two rotors spin very fast, about 2,400 times a minute.

components.label: Rotors
components.description: Two sets of 1.2-metre blades spinning in opposite directions, about 2,400 times a minute, so the helicopter does not twist round.

components.label: Solar panel
components.description: Charges the batteries from sunlight during the day.

components.label: Body (fuselage)
components.description: A small box holding the batteries, the flight computer and heaters to survive the cold nights.

components.label: Landing legs
components.description: Four springy carbon-fibre legs that soften each landing.

components.label: Cameras
components.description: A black-and-white camera looking down to track the ground, and a colour camera for photos.

iss_nasa_v1.title: International Space Station
iss_nasa_v1.summary: A science laboratory orbiting about 400 km above Earth, built by many countries. Astronauts have lived on it continuously since 2000; it goes round the Earth about every 90 minutes.

juno_nasa_v1.title: Juno Spacecraft
juno_nasa_v1.summary: A spacecraft orbiting Jupiter since 2016. Its three huge solar panels make it the farthest solar-powered spacecraft.
juno_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: NASA's own 3D model. It is one solid piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

jupiter_nasa_v1.title: Planet Jupiter
jupiter_nasa_v1.summary: The biggest planet, a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Its stripes are bands of clouds.
jupiter_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: Jupiter
components.description: The biggest planet, a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Its stripes are bands of clouds.
facts: The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth.
It has 95 known moons.

jwst_nasa_v1.title: James Webb Space Telescope
jwst_nasa_v1.summary: The largest space telescope, launched in 2021. Its gold mirror is 6.5 metres across and it sees infrared light from the first galaxies.
jwst_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: NASA's 3D model of Webb. It is one solid piece, so you can turn and zoom it but not pick separate parts.

kepler_nasa_v1.title: Kepler Space Telescope
kepler_nasa_v1.summary: A space telescope (2009–2018) that found thousands of planets around other stars by watching stars dim slightly when a planet passed in front.

mammoth_si_v1.title: Woolly Mammoth Skeleton
mammoth_si_v1.summary: A relative of elephants that lived in cold Ice Age grasslands and died out about 4,000 years ago. This is a real fossil skeleton scanned by the Smithsonian.
mammoth_si_v1.fidelity_note: A 3D scan of the real museum object (Smithsonian). It is one piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

mars_nasa_v1.title: Planet Mars
mars_nasa_v1.summary: The red planet, fourth from the Sun. Its red colour comes from iron oxide (rust) in its dust.
mars_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: Mars
components.description: The red planet, fourth from the Sun. Its red colour comes from iron oxide (rust) in its dust.
facts: It has the tallest volcano in the Solar System, Olympus Mons.
A day on Mars is about 24 hours 37 minutes.

milky_way_v1.title: The Milky Way Galaxy
milky_way_v1.summary: Our galaxy: a huge spinning disk of 100 to 400 billion stars with gas and dust, about 100,000 light years across. The Sun is one of its stars.
milky_way_v1.fidelity_note: Schematic model based on maps of the Milky Way. Nobody can photograph our galaxy from outside, so this is how astronomers picture it; it shows a few thousand dots for hundreds of billions of stars.

components.label: Central bulge
components.description: A crowded ball of mostly old, yellowish stars at the centre of the galaxy.

components.label: Central bar
components.description: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy: a long bar of stars crosses its middle.

components.label: Spiral arms
components.description: Curved arms where gas is squeezed together and new, hot blue stars are born. The pink spots are glowing clouds of gas (nebulae) where stars form.
components.function: Where most new stars are born.
facts: The two biggest arms are called Scutum–Centaurus and Perseus.

components.label: Sagittarius A* (central black hole)
components.description: A supermassive black hole at the very centre, about 4 million times the mass of the Sun.
facts: Its first image was released in 2022 by the Event Horizon Telescope.

components.label: The Sun (you are here)
components.description: Our Sun, about 26,000 light years from the centre, in a small arm called the Orion Spur. It takes about 230 million years to go once round the galaxy.

components.label: Halo
components.description: A faint sphere around the disk with about 150 globular clusters, round balls of very old stars. Most of the galaxy's mass is invisible dark matter, spread through the halo.

mitochondrion_v1.title: Mitochondrion
mitochondrion_v1.summary: The organelle that releases energy from food. Its folded inner membrane gives lots of room for the energy-making machinery.
mitochondrion_v1.fidelity_note: Schematic model, cut open. Real mitochondria are about 1-2 micrometres long and change shape.

components.label: Outer membrane
components.description: The smooth outer skin of the mitochondrion.

components.label: Inner membrane (cristae)
components.description: A second membrane folded into ridges called cristae. The folds give a large surface for making ATP.
facts: Folding packs much more membrane into a small space.

components.label: Intermembrane space
components.description: The narrow gap between the two membranes.

components.label: Matrix
components.description: The thick fluid inside the inner membrane, where food molecules are broken down.

components.label: Mitochondrial DNA
components.description: A small ring of DNA. Mitochondria carry some of their own genes.
facts: You inherit your mitochondrial DNA from your mother.

components.label: Ribosomes
components.description: Tiny protein-builders inside the matrix.

moon_nasa_v1.title: The Moon
moon_nasa_v1.summary: Earth's only natural satellite. The dark patches are 'seas' of old lava; the bright areas are highlands full of craters.
moon_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: The Moon
components.description: Earth's only natural satellite. The dark patches are 'seas' of old lava; the bright areas are highlands full of craters.
facts: The same side always faces Earth.
Twelve astronauts walked on it between 1969 and 1972.

neptune_nasa_v1.title: Planet Neptune
neptune_nasa_v1.summary: The farthest planet from the Sun, an icy giant with the fastest winds in the Solar System.
neptune_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: Neptune
components.description: The farthest planet from the Sun, an icy giant with the fastest winds in the Solar System.
facts: One year on Neptune is about 165 Earth years.

nuclear_reactor_pwr_v1.title: Nuclear Power Plant (PWR)
nuclear_reactor_pwr_v1.summary: A pressurised-water reactor: heat from splitting uranium makes steam, which spins a turbine to make electricity.
nuclear_reactor_pwr_v1.fidelity_note: Schematic cutaway of a pressurised-water reactor (the most common type). Not a model of any real plant; parts simplified and not to scale.

components.label: Containment building
components.description: A thick steel-and-concrete dome around the reactor that keeps radiation in.

components.label: Reactor pressure vessel
components.description: A thick steel tank holding the core and the water around it under very high pressure.

components.label: Fuel core
components.description: Rods of uranium fuel. Uranium-235 nuclei split (fission), releasing a lot of heat.
facts: 1 kg of uranium-235 can release about as much energy as burning ~2,700 tonnes of coal.

components.label: Control rods
components.description: Rods that soak up neutrons. Lowering them slows the chain reaction; raising them speeds it up.

components.label: Primary coolant loop
components.description: Water pumped through the core takes the heat away. High pressure stops it boiling.

components.label: Pressuriser
components.description: Keeps the primary water at high pressure so it stays liquid even at about 300 °C.

components.label: Steam generator
components.description: Hot primary water passes through tubes and boils separate water into steam, without the two mixing.

components.label: Turbine
components.description: Steam pushes on blades and spins the turbine.

components.label: Generator
components.description: The spinning turbine turns a generator, which makes electricity.

components.label: Condenser
components.description: Cools the used steam back into water so it can be pumped round again.

components.label: Cooling tower
components.description: Gets rid of waste heat. The cloud you see is water vapour, not smoke.

perseverance_nasa_v1.title: Perseverance Mars Rover
perseverance_nasa_v1.summary: NASA's rover that landed in Jezero Crater on Mars in February 2021 to look for signs of ancient life and collect rock samples.
perseverance_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: NASA's own 3D model of the rover. Parts are named from the model's own pieces.

components.label: Body (chassis)
components.description: The rover's main box. It holds the computers and electronics and keeps them warm in the freezing Martian nights.

components.label: Remote sensing mast
components.description: A tall neck that lifts the rover's main cameras about 2 metres above the ground, so it can see far like a person standing up.

components.label: Mastcam-Z cameras
components.description: Two zoomable colour cameras side by side, like a pair of eyes. Together they take 3D pictures and video of the landscape.

components.label: Navigation cameras
components.description: Cameras that help the rover and its drivers on Earth plan a safe path to drive.

components.label: Robotic arm
components.description: A 2.1-metre arm with five joints, like a shoulder, elbow and wrist. It holds science tools against rocks.

components.label: Turret (tool hand)
components.description: The 'hand' at the end of the arm. It carries a drill, cameras and instruments, and turns to pick the right tool.

components.label: Coring drill
components.description: Drills out rock cores about the size of a piece of chalk. They are sealed in tubes so a future mission could bring them to Earth.

components.label: PIXL
components.description: An X-ray instrument that finds which chemical elements are in a rock, in spots as small as a grain of salt.

components.label: WATSON camera
components.description: A close-up camera that photographs the tiny textures of rocks, like a magnifying glass.

components.label: Wheels
components.description: Six aluminium wheels, each about 52 cm across, with treads to grip sand and rock.

components.label: Rocker-bogie suspension
components.description: Legs that let each wheel move up and down, so the rover can roll over rocks and keep all six wheels on the ground.

components.label: Power source (MMRTG)
components.description: Turns heat from naturally decaying plutonium-238 into about 110 watts of electricity, day and night. Its heat also keeps the rover warm.

components.label: High-gain antenna
components.description: A flat dish-like antenna that points at Earth to talk to it directly.

components.label: UHF antenna
components.description: Sends most of the rover's pictures to spacecraft orbiting Mars, which pass them on to Earth.

components.label: Low-gain antenna
components.description: A slower antenna that works in any direction, used as a back-up.

components.label: Hazard cameras
components.description: Cameras low on the front and back that spot rocks, holes and slopes so the rover does not drive into danger.

components.label: RIMFAX radar
components.description: A ground-penetrating radar that 'sees' rock layers under the surface as the rover drives.

components.label: Microphones
components.description: Perseverance carried microphones that recorded sounds on Mars, including wind and its own wheels.

components.label: Name chips
components.description: Three small silicon chips carrying 10.9 million names that people on Earth sent to Mars.

photosynthesis_v1.title: Photosynthesis
photosynthesis_v1.summary: Green plants use sunlight to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, giving out oxygen: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
photosynthesis_v1.fidelity_note: Animated diagram: a leaf and its chloroplasts, simplified. Molecules are drawn as coloured balls.

components.label: Sunlight
components.description: Light energy from the Sun is captured by chlorophyll.

components.label: Leaf
components.description: The plant's food factory. It is broad and flat to catch light.

components.label: Chloroplasts
components.description: Tiny green organelles in leaf cells that contain chlorophyll; photosynthesis happens here.

components.label: Stomata
components.description: Tiny pores under the leaf that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.

components.label: Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
components.description: Taken from the air through the stomata.

components.label: Water (H₂O)
components.description: Taken up by the roots and carried up the stem in tubes called xylem.

components.label: Glucose
components.description: The sugar made by the leaf. It is food for the plant, and stored as starch.

components.label: Oxygen (O₂)
components.description: Released into the air as a by-product. This is the oxygen we breathe.

pluto_nasa_v1.title: Dwarf Planet Pluto
pluto_nasa_v1.summary: A dwarf planet beyond Neptune. NASA's New Horizons flew past it in 2015 and found a heart-shaped plain of ice.
pluto_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: Dwarf Pluto
components.description: A dwarf planet beyond Neptune. NASA's New Horizons flew past it in 2015 and found a heart-shaped plain of ice.
facts: It was called the ninth planet until 2006.

respiratory_bp3d_v1.title: Human Respiratory System
respiratory_bp3d_v1.fidelity_note: Anatomical model (BodyParts3D). Colours are a teaching convention.

components.label: Trachea (windpipe)
components.description: The windpipe: a tube held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage. It carries air from the throat down into the chest.

components.label: Bronchi
components.description: The trachea splits into two bronchi, one for each lung. Inside the lungs they keep branching into smaller and smaller tubes (bronchioles).

components.label: Right lung: upper lobe
components.description: The right lung has three lobes. This is the top one.

components.label: Right lung: middle lobe
components.description: Only the right lung has a middle lobe.

components.label: Right lung: lower lobe
components.description: The bottom lobe of the right lung, resting on the diaphragm.

components.label: Left lung: upper lobe
components.description: The left lung has only two lobes, leaving room for the heart. This is the upper one.

components.label: Left lung: lower lobe
components.description: The lower lobe of the left lung.

components.label: Diaphragm
components.description: A dome-shaped sheet of muscle under the lungs. When it contracts and flattens, the chest gets bigger and air is pulled in; when it relaxes, air is pushed out.

saturn_nasa_v1.title: Planet Saturn
saturn_nasa_v1.summary: A gas giant with bright rings made of countless pieces of ice and rock.
saturn_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: Saturn
components.description: A gas giant with bright rings made of countless pieces of ice and rock.
facts: It is so light it would float in a big enough bath of water.
Rings drawn here are a simple illustration.

saturn_v_nasa_v1.title: Saturn V Rocket
saturn_v_nasa_v1.summary: The giant rocket that launched the Apollo missions to the Moon. It was about 110 metres tall and burned its three stages one after another, dropping each empty stage.

shark_si_v1.title: Bignose Shark
shark_si_v1.summary: A shark species (Carcharhinus altimus) from warm deep waters. Sharks are fish whose skeletons are made of cartilage, not bone.
shark_si_v1.fidelity_note: A 3D scan of the real museum object (Smithsonian). It is one piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

shuttle_discovery_si_v1.title: Space Shuttle Discovery
shuttle_discovery_si_v1.summary: A reusable spaceplane that flew 39 missions between 1984 and 2011, including launching the Hubble Space Telescope.
shuttle_discovery_si_v1.fidelity_note: A 3D scan of the real museum object (Smithsonian). It is one piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

skeleton_bp3d_v1.title: Human Skeleton
skeleton_bp3d_v1.fidelity_note: Anatomical model (BodyParts3D). Colours are a teaching convention.

components.label: Skull (cranium and face)
components.description: Eight cranial bones fused into a box that protects the brain, and thirteen face bones (the lower jaw is shown separately). They meet at immovable joints called sutures.

components.label: Lower jaw (mandible)
components.description: The only bone of the skull that moves, at a hinge joint in front of each ear, for chewing and speaking.

components.label: Hyoid bone
components.description: A small U-shaped bone in the neck below the jaw. It touches no other bone; the tongue's muscles are attached to it.

components.label: Neck vertebrae (cervical, 7)
components.description: The seven vertebrae of the neck. The first two, the atlas and the axis, form the pivot joint that lets the head turn from side to side.

components.label: Chest vertebrae (thoracic, 12)
components.description: The twelve vertebrae of the chest. Each pair of ribs is joined to one of them at the back.

components.label: Lower back vertebrae (lumbar, 5)
components.description: The five largest vertebrae, in the lower back. They carry the weight of the whole upper body.

components.label: Sacrum
components.description: Five vertebrae fused into one triangular bone at the base of the spine. It joins the two hip bones to make the pelvis.

components.label: Discs between the vertebrae (cartilage)
components.description: Pads of cartilage between the vertebrae. They cushion the spine and let it bend, a little at each joint.

components.label: Ribs (12 pairs)
components.description: Twelve pairs of curved bones that protect the heart and lungs. The top seven pairs join the breastbone directly (true ribs), the next three join it through cartilage (false ribs), and the last two are free at the front (floating ribs).

components.label: Breastbone (sternum)
components.description: The flat bone at the front of the chest, where the ribs meet. It is made of three pieces: the manubrium, the body and the xiphoid process.

components.label: Rib cartilages (costal)
components.description: Bars of cartilage joining the ribs to the breastbone. Being flexible, they let the chest rise and fall when we breathe.

components.label: Collarbone (clavicle) (right and left)
components.description: A long S-shaped bone across the top of the chest, from the breastbone to the shoulder. It holds the arm out from the body.

components.label: Shoulder blade (scapula) (right and left)
components.description: A flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder. Its shallow socket takes the head of the humerus at the shoulder's ball-and-socket joint.

components.label: Upper arm bone (humerus) (right and left)
components.description: The long bone of the upper arm, from the shoulder to the elbow.

components.label: Radius (right and left)
components.description: The forearm bone on the thumb side. It rolls round the ulna to turn the palm up or down.

components.label: Ulna (right and left)
components.description: The forearm bone on the little-finger side. Its hooked top end makes the point of the elbow and the elbow's hinge joint.

components.label: Wrist bones (carpals, 8 each) (right and left)
components.description: Eight small bones in two rows at the wrist, which glide over one another so the wrist can bend and turn.

components.label: Palm bones (metacarpals, 5 each) (right and left)
components.description: Five long bones in the palm, one leading to each finger.

components.label: Finger bones (phalanges, 14 each) (right and left)
components.description: Three bones in each finger and two in the thumb, joined by hinge joints.

components.label: Hip bone (pelvic girdle) (right and left)
components.description: Each hip bone is three bones fused together (ilium, ischium and pubis). With the sacrum they make the pelvis, which holds up the organs of the abdomen. Its deep socket takes the head of the femur at the hip's ball-and-socket joint.

components.label: Thigh bone (femur) (right and left)
components.description: The longest and strongest bone in the body, from the hip to the knee.

components.label: Kneecap (patella) (right and left)
components.description: A small flat bone at the front of the knee, inside the tendon of the thigh muscle. It protects the knee joint.

components.label: Shin bone (tibia) (right and left)
components.description: The larger bone of the lower leg, on the inner side. It carries the body's weight from the knee to the ankle.

components.label: Fibula (right and left)
components.description: The thin bone on the outer side of the lower leg. It carries little weight; muscles are attached to it, and its lower end makes the outer bump of the ankle.

components.label: Ankle and heel bones (tarsals, 7 each) (right and left)
components.description: Seven bones at the ankle and the back of the foot. The largest, the calcaneus, is the heel; the talus joins the foot to the leg.

components.label: Foot bones (metatarsals, 5 each) (right and left)
components.description: Five long bones in the middle of the foot, one leading to each toe. With the tarsals they make the arch of the foot.

components.label: Toe bones (phalanges, 14 each) (right and left)
components.description: Three bones in each toe and two in the big toe.

skylab_nasa_v1.title: Skylab Space Station
skylab_nasa_v1.summary: America's first space station (1973–79), where three crews lived and did experiments.
skylab_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: NASA's own 3D model. It is one solid piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

solar_system_v1.title: Solar System
solar_system_v1.summary: The Sun and the eight planets that orbit it.
solar_system_v1.fidelity_note: Teaching layout: sizes and distances cannot both be to scale on one screen. Tap 'True sizes' to see the planets' real sizes compared with each other.

components.label: Sun
components.description: Our star: a huge ball of hot gas that gives light and heat to all the planets.
facts: It holds 99.8% of the Solar System's mass.

components.label: Mercury
components.description: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun. A year there is only 88 Earth days.

components.label: Venus
components.description: The hottest planet (about 465 °C), because its thick carbon dioxide air traps heat.
facts: It spins backwards compared with most planets.

components.label: Earth
components.description: Our home, the only planet known to have life and liquid water on its surface.
facts: It has one Moon.

components.label: Mars
components.description: The red planet: its soil has iron oxide (rust). It has the tallest volcano, Olympus Mons.
facts: Perseverance rover is exploring it.

components.label: Jupiter
components.description: The largest planet, a gas giant. Its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth.
facts: It has 95 known moons.

components.label: Saturn
components.description: A gas giant famous for its bright rings of ice and rock.
facts: It is less dense than water.

components.label: Uranus
components.description: An ice giant that spins tipped on its side.

components.label: Neptune
components.description: The farthest planet, an ice giant with the fastest winds in the Solar System.

spacesuit_nasa_v1.title: Spacesuit (EVA suit)
spacesuit_nasa_v1.summary: A spacesuit is a tiny spacecraft for one person: it gives oxygen, keeps the right pressure and temperature, and protects from radiation and tiny meteoroids during spacewalks.
spacesuit_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: NASA's own 3D model. It is one solid piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

spitzer_nasa_v1.title: Spitzer Space Telescope
spitzer_nasa_v1.summary: An infrared space telescope (2003–2020). Infrared light lets it see through dust to stars being born.
spitzer_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: NASA's own 3D model. It is one solid piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

triceratops_si_v1.title: Triceratops Skeleton
triceratops_si_v1.summary: A plant-eating dinosaur with three horns and a bony frill, living about 68–66 million years ago. This is a real fossil skeleton scanned by the Smithsonian.
triceratops_si_v1.fidelity_note: A 3D scan of the real museum object (Smithsonian). It is one piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

trilobite_si_v1.title: Trilobite Fossil
trilobite_si_v1.summary: Trilobites were sea animals with hard, jointed shells, related to insects and crabs. They lived for about 270 million years and died out 252 million years ago.
trilobite_si_v1.fidelity_note: A 3D scan of the real museum object (Smithsonian). It is one piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

urinary_bp3d_v1.title: Human Excretory (Urinary) System
urinary_bp3d_v1.fidelity_note: Anatomical model (BodyParts3D). Colours are a teaching convention.

components.label: Right kidney
components.description: A bean-shaped organ that filters the blood, removing waste and extra water as urine. Each kidney has about a million tiny filters called nephrons.

components.label: Left kidney
components.description: The left kidney sits a little higher than the right one, which is pushed down by the liver.

components.label: Ureters
components.description: Two thin tubes that carry urine from the kidneys down to the bladder.

components.label: Urinary bladder
components.description: A stretchy muscular bag that stores urine until it is passed out.

components.label: Urethra
components.description: The tube through which urine leaves the body.

components.label: Abdominal aorta
components.description: The main artery bringing blood to the kidneys to be cleaned.

components.label: Inferior vena cava
components.description: The large vein carrying cleaned blood away from the kidneys back to the heart.

venus_nasa_v1.title: Planet Venus
venus_nasa_v1.summary: The hottest planet, wrapped in thick clouds. Under them its carbon dioxide air traps heat (about 465 °C).
venus_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: A real NASA map of the surface wrapped on a sphere. Tilt and spin speed are shown for teaching; sizes are not to scale with other bodies.

components.label: Venus
components.description: The hottest planet, wrapped in thick clouds. Under them its carbon dioxide air traps heat (about 465 °C).
facts: It spins backwards, very slowly: a day there is longer than its year.

voyager_nasa_v1.title: Voyager Space Probe
voyager_nasa_v1.summary: Two Voyager probes launched in 1977 flew past the giant planets. Voyager 1 is now the farthest human-made object, in interstellar space, still sending signals with its big dish antenna.
voyager_nasa_v1.fidelity_note: NASA's own 3D model. It is one solid piece: turn and zoom it to look closely.

water_cycle_v1.title: The Water Cycle
water_cycle_v1.summary: Water keeps moving between the sea, the air and the land, powered by the Sun.
water_cycle_v1.fidelity_note: Animated diagram: a simplified landscape, not to scale.

components.label: Sun
components.description: The Sun's heat powers the whole cycle.

components.label: Ocean
components.description: Most of Earth's water is in the oceans.

components.label: Evaporation
components.description: The Sun warms water, which turns into invisible water vapour and rises.

components.label: Transpiration
components.description: Plants give off water vapour from their leaves.

components.label: Condensation
components.description: High up it is cold, so vapour turns into tiny droplets that form clouds.

components.label: Precipitation
components.description: When droplets grow heavy they fall as rain, snow or hail.

components.label: Collection (runoff)
components.description: Rain flows over land into rivers and lakes and back to the sea; some soaks in as groundwater.
